findings.smell: N+1 anti-pattern: claimsOfCell SELECTs ALL tenant claims then filters in JS
findings.risk: At 1M claims, every graph://claims?cell= request materialises the entire tenant claims table into the server process and runs a JS predicate per row. Single-cell read becomes O(tenant) instead of O(cell). Under concurrent readers the server burns CPU + heap proportional to total tenant size, not request scope. Memory pressure and latency scale with the wrong axis.

findings.smell: ReverseIndex built from one cell's claims only — 'referenciado por' is structurally incomplete
findings.risk: buildReverseIndexStatic(claims ?? []) receives only the currently selected cell's ClaimRecord[]. Spec 003 §1 demands O(edges) over the SNAPSHOT. A referrer in cell B pointing into cell A is invisible when A is open — the user reads 'nenhum referenciado' even when referrers exist. The feature's core promise (reverse provenance) is silently wrong for any cross-cell ref graph. The cell-scope rebuild also re-runs O(c*refs) on every cell switch with no reuse.

findings.smell: Hash-routing / query-routing mismatch: filter hydration reads location.search while the app routes via location.hash
findings.risk: App.vue router sets window.location.hash (store.ts:212); HistoryView mounts and reads window.location.search for ?user=&target=&kind=. Shareable filter links (acceptance 06) never load — the URL is always empty here, so deep-links silently drop filters. The acceptance criterion is unmet yet the DoD was flipped to [x].

findings.smell: navigateToClaim cross-cell deferral leaves the leitura→escrita DoD path broken for the documented ref-graph case
findings.risk: TDD-OUTPUT adaptation 08 explicitly defers cross-cell RefChip navigation to 'Phase B' with only a toast. DoD item 1 ('navegar por ref') was checked [x] anyway. A user clicking a RefChip whose target lives outside the loaded cell gets 'ref não encontrado' + a snapshot re-fetch every click — no path to the target claim exists this phase. The closure of the read→write cycle that the feature is named for is conditional on an unfunded Phase B.

findings.smell: Module-level setInterval(pollWho) and setInterval(projectPresence) never cleared
findings.risk: Two setInterval timers start at module load and have no clearInterval on disconnect or HMR dispose. A user who disconnects, closes the tab background, or triggers HMR retains ghost timers polling presence.who against a dead handle every 10s — accumulating 401/network errors and preventing GC of the handle closure. Long-running tabs leak timers proportional to module reloads.

findings.smell: Module-level mutable debounce timer + callCounter + window.__og_query_call_count global
findings.risk: let debounce is shared across any QueryBar instance — under React StrictMode double-mount or HMR the second mount's onChange clears the first's timer mid-flight. window.__og_query_call_count is test instrumentation shipped to production; e2e assertions about debounce sizing leak into the runtime global namespace. Call-counter also races across concurrent keystroke bursts since setTimeout closure captures stale counter value.

findings.smell: God module: 557 lines fold connection + presence + ghosts + toasts + turns + claims + query + history + reverse-index into one file
findings.risk: SRP breach. Every UI-3 concern (and all UI-2 turn logic) lives in og.ts — any change to one vertical re-imports the whole graph. Unit testing the read vertical in isolation requires mocking connect/PresenceStore/GhostStore. Future verticals (Phase B cross-cell nav, draft-after-commit) will pile in here too. The 'ponytail: pure function in reverse-index.ts' extraction is the only seam — every other concern is unextracted.

findings.smell: No pagination / cursor for graph://history?limit=1000 hardcoded — client-side filter over bounded slice
findings.risk: HistoryView hardcodes limit=1000 and filters in-memory. A tenant with 10k+ events shows the latest 1000 only — older events are silently unreachable. The spec acceptance says 'query strings update URL' but there is no since-cursor control exposed to the user; the audit surface is incomplete by default. Memory: holding 1k envelopes + their payloads in zustand forever.

findings.smell: navigateToClaim fallback triggers full loadSnapshot() on every dangling ref
findings.risk: A missing refId (stale snapshot, or any malformed ref string a claim carries) fires loadSnapshot — which re-reads graph://snapshot + graph://changesets?status=open, re-runs loadOpenChangesets with per-cs refetchDeltas. Adversarial or buggy ref content can thrash the snapshot pipeline. No debounce, no negative cache, no 'last refetch timestamp' guard. Cost is unbounded per click.

findings.smell: resolveResource tenant parameter defaults to DEFAULT_TENANT
findings.risk: If a caller forgets to thread the authenticated tenant, the resolver happily serves the default tenant's data. Defense-in-depth missing: the resource layer trusts the caller instead of deriving tenant from a verified token. Spec WD5 calls server 'not frozen' — but read paths should still refuse cross-tenant reads by default, not fall back to a known tenant.

NULL levels are silently coerced to '5' inside the filter, hiding upstream data-quality issues in the claims table. A dangling row with NULL level still matches cells at level 5 — readers see phantom claims they did not commit. The fallback should be explicit reject, not a guessed default.

findings.smell: Mine-set smuggled into the Tree via (out as any).__mine — non-typed side channel on a typed Map
findings.risk: buildTree returns Tree<Map> but hides a Set<string> under an any-cast key. Consumers must know to filter '__mine' out of domain iteration (sidebar-tree.tsx:70) and to read the side channel separately. DRY/typing breach: any future Tree consumer forgets the filter and renders '__mine' as a domain. The mine-set should be a return tuple, not a hidden field.

openPoints: If 50 tenants each hold 20k claims, what is the P99 latency and RSS of a single graph://claims?cell=auth:P4 read — and when does that exceed the SSE heartbeat budget?
How does 'referenciado por' remain truthful when the reverse index is built from one cell's claims but the spec derivation promised a snapshot-wide O(edges) walk?
Why was the cross-cell RefChip navigation deferred to an unfunded Phase B while the DoD checkbox asserting it was flipped to [x]?
If the app routes via location.hash, what is the user-visible behaviour when a HistoryView filter deep-link (?user=bob&kind=changeset.committed) is opened cold?
What bounds the cost of navigateToClaim when a claim carries a malformed ref string — and why is the full loadSnapshot on the failure path considered acceptable per click?
When og.ts grows to absorb Phase B (cross-cell nav, draft-after-commit), at what line count does the god-module become un-maintainable — and what is the extraction seam you wish you had built now?
The two setInterval timers in og.ts run forever after disconnect — what production incident taught you that background tabs poll indefinitely, and why is no clearInterval wired on onClose?

Why is test instrumentation (window.__og_query_call_count) shipped to the production global namespace — and what does its presence in the bundle say about the boundary between e2e harness and app code?
